first_impression.reaction: Intro is fine, not gushing. The takeaways have a dated Smartraveller rating, so I kept going. Went to the FAQ first: short, straight answers, and the legal one doesn't overpromise. Then the Australians section, then skimmed the customs.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Exercise normal safety precautions" in Japan, with a higher level only for the restricted areas near the Fukushima Dai-ichi nuclear power plant.
journey.reaction: Dated, specific, and it names the exception. I'll check it against Smartraveller and I expect it'll match.

journey.section: What a traditional Japanese wedding looks like today
journey.quote: Customs vary from family to family and region to region, and between Shinto, chapel and civil-only weddings.
journey.reaction: Good. Not pretending there's one correct version they can package up and sell me.

journey.quote: Allow generous dressing time between them: a shiromuku takes far longer to put on than a gown.
journey.reaction: Practical trade-off stated plainly. Two ceremonies, two looks, more time. That's the sort of thing that blows out a run sheet and a dresser's invoice.

journey.section: 9. Speeches and the bride's letter to her parents
journey.quote: Near the end of the evening comes the moment that brings the room to tears.
journey.reaction: Bit of a tearjerker line. Doesn't bother me much in a culture piece, but it's the kind of thing I skim past.

journey.quote: Severe heat waves can affect Japan between July and September, and the typhoon season runs from May to November, with most activity between July and September.
journey.reaction: Downsides of the calendar up front, with months. That's what I want before I lock a date and fly 120 people over.

journey.quote: Does a shrine or chapel ceremony register the marriage, or must you also register it at the municipal office?
journey.reaction: That's the catch question for Japan, and they've put it on the list rather than glossing over it. I'd rather have the answer, but a clear list of who to ask is workable.

journey.quote: They work in your time zone and quote in AUD, the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing before any work begins is the right signal, and saying the municipal office, Embassy and shrine set their own steps is honest about scope. Still no word on whether they take a cut from the venue or vendors.

journey.section: Planning your Japanese wedding with us
journey.quote: When you are ready to talk through dates, places or a wedding at home, tell us your date, your guest list and the feeling you want, and a Wedded Advisor will start from there.
journey.reaction: 'The feeling you want' is a bit soft for me. Tell me what the first call covers and whether it costs anything, and I'm more likely to book it.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues, dressers, kimono hire and other vendors?
What does the Wedded Advisor fee cover and how is it calculated?
Is the first conversation with a Wedded Advisor free, and what does it cover?
Have they planned a wedding in Japan, and is there a real example with the actual budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Japanese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Clickbait headline, and the article is better than it. Title was set by the person, so noted only.

turn_offs_found.quote: A Japanese wedding asks for careful timing: two families, two ceremonies, several outfits and a room ready for a letter that will make everyone cry.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional sign-off where I want the practical next step. Minor.

would_share_with: My partner, for the legal steps questions and the typhoon and heat timing
Her parents, to check which customs their family actually keeps and how they feel about yuinō

cta_reaction.quote: They work in your time zone and quote in AUD, the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the evidence, not before, and the written fee line is what I look for. I'd still look for a fees or commissions page before handing over my details.

top_3_changes: In the closing section, swap 'the feeling you want' for what the first call covers and whether it's free.
Trim the emotional sign-off ('a letter that will make everyone cry') to a plainer line about the next step.
Say, even in one line, whether the Wedded Advisor takes commissions or mark-ups from suppliers (business detail deferred, so nice-to-have).
